text:
anya: Spot check: console p95 for /v1/embeddings jumped at 09:22 but raw logs show a tiny routing cohort (fallback-router) had 7 requests, all slow. The merged p95 reads 180ms which is alarming on the surface.

ben: Yeah that's the recurring problem. We show only the merged percentile in the SLO header and people page it. Need per-cohort provenance.

kai: Quick proposal: show a compact "provenance" row under each percentile: origin=count (e.g. router-fallback=7, client=12k). If any origin < threshold, mark percentile as low-confidence.

anya: Also request: tie the console alerting rules to min_sample_count. Currently we fire p95 alerts solely on merged value; add a gating rule that suppresses alerts when total_count < 50 or when merged p95 CI is > 2x median.

ben: Implementation detail: computing accurate merged p95 requires concatenating sketches or raw samples. Do not implement naive weighted-mean of p95s. We'll add an API param include_origins=true that returns rows with origin,p50,p95,p99,count, and a merged entry with p95_ci.

kai: UI: inline small icon with tooltip: "merged percentile includes small cohorts — click to expand per-origin rows". Also a slider for min_count to hide cohorts smaller than X.

ops-bot: deploybot: routing-fallback-adjust 2025-07-01T09:20:00Z rolled out to staging (15%).

anya: I'll open a short RFC for the alert gating and the API change. Goal: reduce misinterpreted p95 regressions and surface root cause faster.

ben: Add a unit test that constructs three cohorts (big fast, big fast, tiny slow) and asserts merged quantile equals quantile of concatenated samples. We should fail fast if someone tries approximate weighting.

kai: I'll draft the design mock and the API contract.

anya: thanks — will link RFC to routing PR.
